newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Afrox buys stake in Zambia firm for $60 mln.
newsitem.headline: Afrox buys stake in Zambia firm for $60 mln.

text.p: African Oxygen Ltd of South Africa on Thursday acquired the majority shareholding in Zambia Oxygen Ltd in an ongoing exercise by the Zambian government to privatise state-run enterprises, the Zambia Privatisation Agency annouced.
Agency chief executive Valentine Chitalu said the South African firm had acquired 70 percent of the company at a package price of $60 million.
The acquired firm is the major manuafacturer and supplier of industrial and medical gases in Zambia and dominates the local market for liquid oxygen, nitrogen and liqud carbon dioxide.
"Afrox has acquired 70 percent of Zamox at a package value of $60 million," Chitalu told a news conference held jointly with Afrox chairman and managing director Royden Vice.
Zamox was a subsidiary of British Oxygen Company Plc, the majority shareholder and parent company of Afrox, before it was nationalised in 1985.
Vice said Afrox would invest around $20 million in capital investment and training in Zamox over the next few years.
"A condition for the acquisition of Zamox is that it will be floated on the Lusaka stock exchange at a future date," Vice said.

He said Afrox intended to make Zamox, whose performance suffered under government control, competitive on the world market. "We belive we will be the number one operation in the central part of Africa," he said.
